summary: This guide explains how to start an orchard or vineyard, covering soil and climate testing, choosing fruit varieties, planting and maintenance, harvest, and turning fruit into wines, spirits, and dishes. It draws on quotes from growers, a winemaker, a sommelier, and a chef, all tied to autumn 2023 dates. It closes with the community role of these farms and the importance of sustainability and innovation.
one_line: A guide to starting an orchard or vineyard, from soil testing and variety choice to harvest, fruit-based products, pairings, and sustainability.
key_facts: Horticulturist Emily Thompson started her orchard in the rolling countryside of Vermont on September 15, 2023, and stresses soil testing for pH, drainage, and soil type.
Choosing fruit varieties is critical: grapes include varietals such as Merlot and Chardonnay, while orchards offer stone fruits like cherries and peaches and pome fruits like pears and apples.
Local agricultural extension services can advise on which crops will thrive in a region, and heritage or heirloom varieties can offer distinct flavors.
Luca Martinez planted his first vines outside Napa Valley on September 10, 2023, and says good spacing allows sunlight and air flow, reducing disease.
Sarah Jensen of Jensen Orchards opened her orchards' gates to the public on September 30, 2023, and her Pick-Your-Own days have been a hit, giving a direct market for produce.
Winemaker Franco DiGiovanni's Syrah, harvested on October 5, 2023, has a bold character with hints of blackberries that grow wild on his property's edges.
Alice Hartford launched a line of apple brandy only six months after her first harvest.
Sommelier Andrew Richardson says a crisp, apple-infused chardonnay can elevate roast pork, and a berry dessert pairs well with a sweet grape-based dessert wine.
Chef Helena Sousa launched an autumn menu on September 22, 2023, featuring a peach-infused duck breast matched with a light-bodied, fruity red wine from a vineyard 10 miles away.
Orchards and vineyards support local tourism and education through wine tasting events and educational tours.
Ted Nelson runs a biodynamic vineyard aimed at a balanced ecosystem and says sustainability is a philosophy of giving back as much as we take.
Sustainability efforts include organic farming practices and new irrigation techniques to meet the challenges of a changing climate.
